assumptions: USD million. Fictional Rowan Yard. Toy landlord-owned improvements PPE, tenant-owned cash incentive deferred and amortized against rent. Full-year rent recognition with contractual concession. No tax.

evidence.text: [Lease A] Annual stated rent24, free first quarter; total earned cash consideration18 over one-year term, evenly recognized. All18 collected. No opening deferred balance.
[Lease B] Five-year lease from Jan1, annual stated rent30, tenant incentive10 paid immediately; straight-line reduction2 per year. Cash rent collected28; all30 billed.
[Improvements] Landlord-owned fit-out15 paid Jan1, five-year life, depreciation3 current. Tenant-owned incentive10 separate deferred asset, not PPE.
[Existing] Opening PPE100, depreciation10 on existing assets. Property cash-type operating expense18, corporate7, interest6. No other income or expense.
[Cash] All listed cash-type expenses paid. Opening cash40, new debt20, principal repayment5. No cash capital addition except fit-out15 and incentive10.
[Metrics] NOI=recognized rent less property operating expense, excludes all D&A. Cash flow incentive payment investing under toy; FCF=CFO less both fit-out and incentive.
[Debt] Opening gross debt80, restricted cash5 unchanged. Net debt uses unrestricted cash only.
[Deck] Adds cash incentive10 to property cost and deducts it all from current rent, treats full lease A stated24 as earned.

qas.answer: Cash rent = 18+28 = 46m; CFO = 46−18−7−6 = 15m. Deduct both landlord fit-out15 and tenant incentive10 per the disclosed metric: FCF = −10m.

Find closing net debt using unrestricted cash.
qas.answer: CFO = 18+28−18−7−6 = 15m. Unrestricted closing cash = 40+15−15−10+20−5−5 = 40m. Gross debt = 80+20−5 = 95m; net debt = 95−40 = 55m.

qas.question: Why not include the entire 10m incentive in current-year rental expense and PPE?
qas.answer: It is tenant-owned incentive consideration, a separate deferred asset amortized over five years; neither landlord PPE nor entirely current expense.

qas.question: Can the property's actual market value be inferred from current NOI28?
qas.answer: No. Need cap rate, market leases, risk and valuation assumptions.
